Why whiskey? It is not going to develop and won't really be any different than a bottle you will be able to buy in 21 years. I'd suggest something like a vintage port, a good high tannin red wine or a high ABV English-style barleywine. With those last two suggestions, you'll need to do research a little to make sure the specific wine or beer can go the distance. If you went with a vintage port, that shouldn't be an issue.

If those interest you, I can make various suggestions if you'd like.

The right wines age spectacularly and get much better with the right amount of age. But 21 years is a pretty long time, so it really cuts into the wines that would be suited to that. For that reason a lot of people buy vintage port for their kids to enjoy as adults. But they do not necessarily release vintages every year depending on how their growing comditions go. So you may not even know if you can get a 2017 vintage port until well towards the end of the year or next year sometime.

If looking at a regular wine, in your price range, I'm a fan of an Italian wine called Mastroberardino Radici Taurasi. I've had them at about 20 years and they've been very good. Of course every vintage is slightly different. There are also tons of good choices from Napa (most likely a Cabernet Sauvignon with strong tannins or a Bordeaux style blend), France (Bordeaux or Burgundy are good places to look at), Spain (some Rioja Gran Reservas can age that long), Italy (Brunellos can age). But a good number of wines which might be expected to be held that long might be more expensive.

If you are interested in beers, you could pick up a few bottles of JW Lees Harvest Ale, which can definitely age for 21 years. Thomas Hardy Ale is perhaps the best for aging that long, but may be harder to get. Fuller's Vintage Ale should have no problem. Sierra Nevada Bigfoot can, too, but opinions are mixed on the effects (I myself have gone back amd forth on the subject even). There are several other ales which I believe can make that journey (North Coast Old Stock Ale, Victory Old Horizontal, Bell's Third Coast Old Ale), but most of them I have so far only pushed to 10 years or so and I would be guessing.
